context: Test shell logic through a deterministic Git-Bash discovery/helper or port pure filters to Python; assert the shell implementation actually ran so a launcher failure cannot masquerade as business-logic output.
description: Run 30434746317 has eight PR workflow classifier failures and one release-branch sweep failure whose subprocess output is UTF-16 'Windows Subsystem for Linux has no installed distributions'. Python subprocess(['bash', ...]) resolves the Windows WSL stub rather than Git Bash, so the tests never exercise the shell snippets.

deferrals.reason: Independent triage of Nightly run 30473819253 (both Windows jobs) found test_validate_submission_changed_bundles.py failing from the same WSL-stub cause (2 failures: test_applied_only_change_discovers_paired_primary_bundle, test_applied_companion_rename_discovers_the_source_primary_bundle), but that file is absent from this item's only_modify list, so a claimant would be blocked from fixing it. Also confirming the mechanism for whoever picks this up: the garbled assertion text is UTF-16LE and decodes to 'Windows Subsystem for Linux ... <Distro> to install.', i.e. bash resolved to C:\\Windows\\System32\\bash.exe (WSL launcher, no distro) and exited 1 - a wrong-interpreter bug, NOT the missing-encoding family it superficially resembles. Git Bash IS on the runner (actions/checkout invokes C:\\Program Files\\Git\\bin\\git.exe), so resolving it explicitly instead of trusting PATH order is viable.
